messages.subject: Re: D5 MRDS
parts:
Sorry for my late reply on this query. My responses are below.

B=F8thun Gjermund wrote:
> > I have two questions about a independent observer (IO) configuration, a=
ssuming point independence (PI?) in the MRDS engine.
> >
> > =20
> >
> > Would it be wrong to include a covariate in the DS model g.(y; theta) t=
hat describe which observer saw the object (the capture history from the =
MR-data) or a covariate describing duplicate/non duplicate?=20
> >
> > =20
I believe this would be wrong because we assume that the distribution of=20
the covariate is independent of distance which is clearly not the case=20
here because they are a product of the result of detection. Another =20
covariate that might be tempting to use would be behavior as a cue for=20
sighting. It would be ok unless the behavior was altered by the=20
observer. For example, if a bird was more likely to dive in response to=20
the an approaching boat vs a bird that is a long distance from the=20
boat. In that case the covariate z is dependent on distance and would=20
not be a valid one to use.
> > Since this is (partly) the MR-data my concern is that the two likelihoo=
ds should be optimized simultaneously and not independently as done by th=
e MRDS engine.=20
> >
> > =20
> > =20
I suggest you look at Chapter 6 in Buckland et al 2004 or Borchers et al=20
2006 in Biometrics. The reason the 2 components can be optimized=20
separately is because they do not share any parameters when the models=20
are for conditional and unconditional detection functions. As we state=20
in Chapter 6, an alternative approach is to model the unconditional=20
detection functions and delta (the measure of distortion from unmodeled=20
heterogeneity) and if you do that then the 2 components of the=20
likelihood are no longer independent because they share parameters. =20
This approach may provide a better modelling tool conceptually but it is=20
a disadvantage numerically because it is a harder optimization problem. =20
We use this alternate approach in a paper that we have submitted to=20
Biometrics.
> > The manual specify that the covariate for a given object must be identi=
cal for the two observers. If you suspect differences between the two ob=
servers would it be possible to include observer as a covariate in the MR=
model p1|2(y; beta)?=20
> >
> > =20
> > =20
Certainly you can use observer (platform) as a covariate in the MR=20
model; but not in the DS model because it is the set of pooled=20
observations. But that is not the same as what is being referred to in=20
the above. It is in reference to covariates like group size or sea=20
state. If these covariates are for the same object why would they=20
differ? It is possible to allow for different covariate values but the=20
code does not allow it currently.

regards --jeff
